summary: Ustaz Azlan tells how the open call began after three years of closed da'wah. The Prophet SAW received the command of Surah Ash-Shu'ara verse 214 to warn his nearest relatives, then held two banquets for Banu Hashim which Abu Lahab spoiled, except that Ali declared his support. The Prophet SAW then climbed Mount Safa and called all of Quraysh, tested their trust with a question about an army behind the hill, delivered a warning, was cursed by Abu Lahab, and Surah Al-Masad came down. The ustaz also covers the effect on the Prophet's SAW daughters and the fate of Abu Lahab and his wife.
keyPoints: The open call began when Allah commanded the Prophet SAW in Ash-Shu'ara 214 to warn his nearest kin.
Calling one's relatives is harder and more painful than calling outsiders.
Abu Lahab spoiled the first banquet; at the second the Prophet SAW recited the khutbat al-hajah and only Ali declared support.
On Mount Safa the Prophet SAW called all the clans, and Quraysh affirmed his honesty before he warned them.
Abu Lahab cursed the Prophet SAW and Surah Al-Masad came down exposing his fate and his wife's.
Abu Lahab's sons divorced Ruqayyah and Umm Kulthum at their father's command, and the Prophet SAW made du'a against Utaybah.
A caller must manage expectations and accept rejection as part of the prophets' path.

chapters.title: Replay of the ending and the opening
chapters.summary: The lecture opens with a clip of the Safa and Abu Lahab ending, then starts the chapter after three years.

chapters.title: Every big thing begins small
chapters.summary: The ustaz shares experiences of a school that began from second-hand wood and advice for young people on patience.

chapters.title: The command of Ash-Shu'ara 214
chapters.summary: The verse commands warning the nearest relatives.

chapters.title: Calling relatives is harder
chapters.summary: Kin hurt the most; only Abu Lahab gets a surah dedicated to him.

chapters.title: Managing expectations and the stories of earlier prophets
chapters.summary: Surah Ash-Shu'ara tells of earlier prophets so the Prophet SAW and companions would not expect to be accepted by all.

chapters.title: The first banquet for Banu Hashim
chapters.summary: Ali prepared goat soup for 45 people; the food sufficed but Abu Lahab broke up the gathering.

chapters.title: The second banquet and the khutbat al-hajah
chapters.summary: The Prophet SAW spoke during the meal, recited the khutbat al-hajah and conveyed prophethood and resurrection.

chapters.title: Family reaction: Abu Talib and Ali
chapters.summary: Abu Talib gave room but would not leave his grandfather's religion; only Ali promised support.

chapters.title: Mount Safa
chapters.summary: The Prophet SAW called all the clans and tested their trust with a question about an army.

chapters.title: The warning and Abu Lahab's departure
chapters.summary: The Prophet SAW called clans and kin by name and said he could not shield anyone from the punishment; Abu Lahab cursed him.

chapters.title: Surah Al-Masad and Abu Lahab
chapters.summary: The meaning of Lahab, changed family ties and the divorce of the Prophet's SAW daughters.

chapters.title: The du'a against Utaybah and Umm Jamil
chapters.summary: Utaybah was killed by a lion; Umm Jamil harmed the Prophet SAW with campaigns and thorns.

chapters.title: Abu Lahab's end and closing
chapters.summary: Abu Lahab died in disgrace; the ustaz closes by reflecting on facing rejection.

people.context: Spoiled the banquet and cursed the Prophet SAW at Safa; a whole surah is dedicated to him.
Sister of Abu Sufyan; harmed the Prophet SAW with campaigns and wicked acts.

people.role: Adopted son of the Prophet SAW, about 10
people.context: Prepared the banquet and was the only one to declare support.
Gave room but did not leave the religion of Abdul Muttalib.
His wife accepted Islam after the banquet.
Divorced Ruqayyah and Umm Kulthum at their father's order; Utaybah was later killed by a lion.
Married to Abu Lahab's sons and then divorced.
Stayed silent when Umm Jamil insulted; Allah veiled his sight so she did not see the Prophet SAW.
Mentioned among the Prophet's SAW enemies but his fate was not decided there.

lessons.title: Start small and be patient
lessons.body: Schools and big institutions begin with small steps; do not rush to leap.

lessons.title: Relatives are the hardest to call
lessons.body: Speaking the truth to family is harder and more painful than to outsiders.

lessons.title: Manage expectations in da'wah
lessons.body: All prophets were opposed; the motivation is conveying for Allah, not being liked.

lessons.title: Offer the best to family first
lessons.body: A good product is offered to family first; otherwise there is a sign of a scam.

lessons.title: Test credibility before delivering
lessons.body: The Prophet SAW had Quraysh affirm his honesty before warning them.

lessons.title: Important news demands action
lessons.body: Naba' is important news that must be conveyed and acted on.

lessons.title: Kinship does not save
lessons.body: The Prophet SAW could not shield Fatimah or his family from punishment; each person chooses.

lessons.title: The pain of a child being humiliated
lessons.body: Public divorce aimed to crush the Prophet's SAW spirit; he retaliated only when his family was harmed.

lessons.title: Handle rejection
lessons.body: Reflect on strategy, resources and how to handle rejection; revisit those we gave up on.

glossary.meaning: The opening sermon the Prophet SAW recited whenever he began a speech.
A morning cry like 'beware, danger' that draws attention.
The Prophet's SAW clan, living in 'section seven'.
A flame; used for Abu Lahab with his reddish face.
An opponent who may still be considered, like Abu Talib and Al-Abbas.

dalil.context: The command to warn the nearest relatives, marking the start of the open call.
Surah Al-Masad came down after Abu Lahab cursed the Prophet SAW at Safa. (reference identified, verse number not stated)
dalil.translation: May the hands of Abu Lahab be ruined! May he be ruined too!

dalil.context: Surah Al-Kawthar came down when Abu Lahab celebrated the death of the Prophet's SAW son with 'cut off'. (reference identified, verse number not stated)
dalil.translation: We have truly given abundance to you [Prophet]––

dalil.context: Surah An-Naba' as great news that demands action, linked to the Prophet's SAW warning. (reference identified, verse number not stated)
Recited by the Prophet SAW at the second banquet; the ustaz recites it at the start of each lecture.
dalil.translation: All praise is for Allah; we praise Him, seek His help, guidance and forgiveness, and seek refuge with Allah from the evil of ourselves and our bad deeds; whoever Allah guides none can misguide; I bear witness there is no god but Allah and that Muhammad is His servant and messenger.

dalil.context: From the sirah narration of Ibn Hisham.
dalil.translation: A leader does not lie to his own people; by Allah I am Allah's messenger to you and to all mankind; you will die as you sleep and be raised as you wake, then be reckoned with, and only eternal Paradise or Hell remain.

dalil.context: The Prophet's SAW speech at Safa, the cry 'Ya Sabahah'.
dalil.translation: If I told you an army was ready behind this hill to attack, would you act? They said yes; then the Prophet SAW said he was a warner of a severe punishment and called on them to save themselves from the Fire.

dalil.context: The Prophet SAW prayed after Utaybah harmed him; Utaybah was later killed by a lion.
dalil.translation: O Allah, set one of Your dogs upon him.

sirah.era: The start of the open call after three years
sirah.summary: The Prophet SAW began calling kin and all of Makkah and faced Abu Lahab's rejection.
